inventory.name: text-decoration-skip-spaces — the CSS property that controls whether text decoration lines (underline, overline, line-through) skip spacers and word separators

syntax.rationale: The anchored slice is the page's property-definition table — the rows a CSS propdef carries, each value in a <td>: Property `text-decoration-skip-spaces` in <code>, Applies to 'All elements', Inherited 'Yes', Initial value 'Determined by UA stylesheet (typically `none` for most browsers)'. Three of those four rows match css-text-decor-4 §2.10.3 as fetched 2026-10-07 (HTTP 200): Name `text-decoration-skip-spaces`, Applies to 'all elements', Inherited 'yes'; the ChromeStatus record's own name field, 'CSS4 text-decoration-skip-spaces' (read 2026-10-07 from the public API endpoint, HTTP 200), corroborates the first row. DIVERGENCE REPORTED, NOT FIXED: the anchored Initial value row states a settled UA-stylesheet default of `none`, while the propdef reads Initial `start end` and carries the unresolved issue 'Should the initial value be none for Web-compat? If not, INS and DEL at least should be assigned none in the UA default stylesheet. See also Issue 4653.'; the fetched Appendix B Default UA Stylesheet assigns no text-decoration-skip-spaces rule at all, so the row presents an open question as a settled fact. OMISSION FROM THE PAGE, NOT A CONTRADICTION: the anchored table carries no Value, Computed value or Animation type row, so the grammar `none | all | [ start || end ]`, Computed value 'specified keyword(s)' and Animation type 'discrete' appear nowhere on the page; the declaration shape as an author writes it is carried by the #syntax slice, which anchors examples.

inputs.rationale: The anchored slice is the list of values an author may write — four keyword rows, each keyword in <code>: `none` ('Decoration lines span the full width including spaces (default behaviour).'), `leading` ('Skip space before the first word (at the start of the inline).'), `trailing` ('Skip space after the last word (at the end of the inline).') and `all` ('Skip all whitespace — leading, trailing, and between words.') — plus the citation line beneath the table. Two of the four are the spec's own keywords, fetched 2026-10-07 (HTTP 200): §2.10.3 defines `none` as 'Spacers are not skipped. They are decorated just like any other character.' and `all` as 'Skip all spacers and all word separators plus any adjacent letter-spacing or word-spacing.'. DIVERGENCE REPORTED, NOT FIXED: `leading` and `trailing` are keywords §2.10.3 does not define — the spec's other two valdefs are `start` and `end` (valdef ids valdef-text-decoration-skip-spaces-start and -end; the fetched document has no -leading or -trailing), and all four WPT samples css/css-text-decor/text-decoration-skip-spaces-001.html through -004.html (fetched 2026-10-07 from web-platform-tests/wpt master, HTTP 200) declare `text-decoration-skip-spaces: start end`. DIVERGENCE REPORTED, NOT FIXED: the anchored citation line reads 'CSS Text Decoration Level 4 §2.10.3', while the property is defined in §2.10.3 and the fetched document's section 5 'Painting Text Decorations' has only §5.1 and §5.2. OMISSIONS FROM THE PAGE, NOT CONTRADICTIONS: no anchored fragment states the grammar `none | all | [ start || end ]` (that `start` and `end` combine), the Initial value `start end`, or the 'spacer' definition — any typographic character unit from Unicode General Category Zs except U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE, with all, start and end also skipping adjacent letter-spacing and word-spacing; the `none` row's '(default behaviour)' is the same Initial-value divergence named above, seen from the value list.

outputs.rationale: The output is a rendering change and the anchored slice shows it twice: two live rows under the same phrase, one with `all` ('each word underlined separately', gaps at the word boundaries) and one with `none` ('continuous underline across spaces'), plus the <pre><code> rules that produce them. Per §2.10.3 the specified effect is that spacers and word separators (plus any adjacent letter-spacing or word-spacing) are not painted under, and the property controls all decoration lines drawn by the element as well as any drawn by its ancestors. A CSS property returns no script-visible value, so the painted result is the whole output surface.

errors.rationale: A declarative CSS property has no exception, rejection or error-code surface: there is no call to fail, so nothing throws and the anchored slice documents no error path. The only failure mode is availability — a browser without the property, or a keyword it does not support, drops the declaration at parse time per standard CSS error handling and paints the decoration as if the declaration were absent. GAP FLAGGED: the page states that dropped-declaration fallback nowhere, and the ChromeStatus record's activation_risks field is null, so neither cited source describes the degradation path either.

context.rationale: Exposure and prerequisites are carried by the anchored support table: Chrome '150 — developer trial (flag required)', Edge 'Tracking Chromium', Firefox 'No signal', Safari 'No signal'. Verified against the record on 2026-10-07 — DevTrial stage_type 230 desktop_first/android_first 150 and flag_name 'enable-experimental-web-platform-features' — so the flag-gated developer-trial prerequisite that cell states is the record's own value, and ff_views 5 / safari_views 5 decode to 'No signal'. GAP FLAGGED, NOT PAPERED OVER: the flag's own URL (chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features, in the page's un-anchored warn-block and at-a-glance table) is outside every anchored fragment, and the element scope (Applies to: all elements; Inherited: yes) is anchored at #the-property for the syntax dimension but sits outside this dimension's #browser-support slice.

lifecycle.rationale: An inherited declarative property has no runtime lifecycle: nothing is constructed, registered, awaited, cancelled or torn down, and its effect is recomputed at each style, layout and paint pass rather than moving through states of its own. The only transitions this page documents are release-availability ones — the anchored table's developer trial in Chrome 150, with the record's Ship stage_type 260 at desktop/android/webview 155 — which belong to the context and compatibility dimensions above, not to a lifecycle of the property.

examples.rationale: The anchored slice carries one complete semantic <pre><code> example — two rules, `.skip-spaces` with `text-decoration-skip-spaces: all` and `.no-skip` with `none`, each beside the `text-decoration: underline` it modifies — plus two rendered rows showing the visual difference, which is what the example claims. The sibling 'recipes' section adds two further <pre><code> rules (link underlines with text-underline-offset and text-decoration-skip-ink; a line-through sale price); it is deliberately NOT anchored, because an id on that <h2> would resolve to an empty fragment (fragmentAfterId() stops at its first <h3>).

compatibility.rationale: Tabular per-engine support, including explicit unknowns: Chrome '150 — developer trial (flag required)', Edge 'Tracking Chromium', Firefox 'No signal', Safari 'No signal', cited to 'chromestatus browser views, May 2026'. Checked against the record on 2026-10-07: DevTrial stage desktop_first/android_first 150, ff_views 5 and safari_views 5 = 'No signal', browsers.chrome.status.text 'Proposed'. UNSOURCED CELL REPORTED, NOT ADJUDICATED: the record carries no Edge-specific field, so 'Tracking Chromium' is Chromium-parity inference rather than a value in the cited source. OMISSION REPORTED: the record's Ship stage (desktop/android/webview 155) is a milestone the table does not mention.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The property changes only where decoration lines are painted across spacers and word separators: it exposes no data, grants no capability, and adds no script-visible state, storage, permission, network or cross-origin surface, and the anchored slice shows nothing but that painting difference. css-text-decor-4's own Privacy Considerations section reads 'No new privacy considerations have been reported on this specification' and its Security Considerations section reads 'No new security considerations have been reported on this specification' (fetched 2026-10-07). NOT CORROBORATED BY THE RECORD, stated rather than smoothed over: ChromeStatus 4832783806627840 carries security_review_status 'Pending' and privacy_review_status 'Pending', so what the record says is that the reviews are unfinished, not that the feature was found clean.
